subject: Equinox: request to secure feature window for confidential-logging control
messages:
From: Jason Miller <jason.miller@equinoxcap.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 13:25:00 -0400
Subject: Production requirement: configurable confidential-logging control for vault-backed keys

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quick follow-up from our security and infra teams: to move forward with a production contract we need a configurable control on server-side logging that can mute or redact start/end tokens and any KV cache identifiers tied to customer data. The ask is twofold:
- a runtime flag or route-level setting we can toggle from our console (or via API) that turns on aggressive logging redaction
- an auditable export showing when that flag was toggled and by whom (retained for 13 months)

Attached is a short mutual action plan (EQ-Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf) that highlights timing constraints — our procurement needs the capability to be in the April engineering window to meet our Q3 launch. If this requires a narrow, gated change (feature window), we need to lock the sprint by April 20.

Can you confirm feasibility and whether this requires a product exception / prioritized slot? Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jason Miller
Head of Platform Engineering
Equinox Capital
jason.miller@equinoxcap.com
+1 617 555 0193

Attachments: EQ-Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf (plan), attachment-stub-soc2-scoped-items.xlsx (requested scope)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Production requirement: configurable confidential-logging control for vault-backed keys

Team — forwarding EQ’s ask. High level: Equinox wants a route/runtime toggle to aggressively redact logs plus an audit export retained for 13 months. They are requesting we target the April engineering window (they need it to ship in Q3).

Asks for Product/Eng:
- Can we scope a minimal implementation that adds a boolean route param (suppress_sensitive_logs) + server-side redactors for tokens/KV-ids?
- What is the estimated effort (S/M/L) and which sprint would be the earliest we could ship a gated flag?
- Does this require changes to telemetry/audit pipeline for 13-month retention and export?

Context: this is a deal acceleration ask tied to a $1.1M ARR commitment on close. Equinox is willing to accept a limited feature flag (customer-scoped) and sign an activation-specific SLA if needed.

Irene — can you triage feasibility? Ben — I'll own the comms with Jason and procurement. Monica — can you add legal/compliance touchpoints if we need to propose an activation SLA or retention exception?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov

olga.petrov@redwood.ai

-- Forwarded attachment: EQ-Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf (map + timelines)
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirement: configurable confidential-logging control for vault-backed keys

Thanks for the heads-up — this is a concrete engineering ask with some tricky parts but likely reasonable as a scoped, gated change. Quick notes from runtime/product perspective:

1) Scoping suggestion (minimal viable change):
   - Add a per-route boolean (suppress_sensitive_logs) checked at request entry. When true, redact token-level traces and any KV cache ids from trace payloads and log lines.
   - Implement redaction as a sanitization pass before logs/telemetry are emitted (rule-based pattern matching + allowlist).
   - Audit events: emit a discrete audit record when the flag is toggled (user, timestamp, route id). Exportable via existing audit export pipeline.

2) Effort estimate & sprint placement:
   - Rough estimate: 5 dev-days + 3 QA-days + 2 infra-days to extend export retention config. (This is a bench-level rough estimate; could change after a spike.)
   - Earliest realistic slot: feature spike in sprint starting Apr 22, gated delivery by May 10 (can be feature-flagged behind a customer allowlist).

3) Risks / blockers:
   - Telemetry pipeline currently defaults to 90-day retention. Extending to 13 months is a config+storage cost and may trigger compliance review (SOC2 evidence).
   - Need legal sign-off on audit export format/PII redaction.

Requesting: a quick 30-min sync with Eng infra + Security to confirm retention path. If we go ahead with Apr 22 spike we should lock sprint by April 18.

I can own the spike & a short RFC. Assigning a small eng owner for the change will reduce turnaround — Ben / Olga, please confirm if we should treat this as a prioritized slot for Equinox and whether procurement is comfortable with a feature-flagged initial delivery.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. PM, Platform
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirement: configurable confidential-logging control for vault-backed keys

Appreciate the quick triage, Irene. Confirming commercial stance: Equinox has verbally committed to $1.1M ARR if we can meet the May pilot readiness target; procurement prefers the April engineering window lock. Legal/Compliance (Monica) — can you advise on whether the 13-month retention is a blocker from an SOC2 / customer contract standpoint?

Operational proposal:
- We approve a sprint spike Apr 22. Irene to own RFC + spike with one eng assignee.
- Delivery as a gated, customer-allowlisted feature by May 10.
- Equinox signs an activation addendum that documents the SLA and the initial limited rollout.

Olga — please set the call with Equinox for Friday (20 min) to confirm acceptance and procurement timelines. I'll prep a short commercial note for the addendum.
